title: Disability
claim_scope: Broad contextual anchor: 1.3 billion people, or 16% of the world population, experienced significant disability in the 2021 estimate; disability is an interaction with contextual factors and is not a format-specific denominator.

title: Nearly 240 million children with disabilities around the world, UNICEF's most comprehensive statistical analysis finds
claim_scope: Almost 240 million children aged 0-17, about one in ten; children with disabilities were 49% more likely never to have attended school than peers without disabilities; relative disparity is not an out-of-school headcount.

title: Seen, Counted, Included: Using data to shed light on the well-being of children with disabilities
claim_scope: Full methodology and cross-country functional-difficulty analysis underlying the almost-240-million child estimate; combines internationally comparable data from 42 countries.

title: Blindness and vision impairment
claim_scope: At least 2.2 billion people have near or distance vision impairment and at least 1 billion cases were preventable or remained unaddressed; broad measure is not a blindness or accessible-format-usage count.

title: Vision Atlas Global Snapshot
organization: International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness and Vision Loss Expert Group / Global Burden of Disease Study
claim_scope: 2020 model: 1.106 billion people with vision loss, comprising approximately 43 million blind, 295 million moderate-to-severe distance loss, 258 million mild distance loss, and 510 million near loss; age distribution 90 million aged 0-19, 213 million aged 20-49, and 802 million aged 50+.

title: Vision Atlas definitions
organization: International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness
claim_scope: Defines blindness as visual acuity worse than 3/60 (20/400) or visual field no greater than 10 degrees in the better eye and supplies severity bands used in the Vision Atlas.

title: Deafness and hearing loss
claim_scope: 430 million people, including 34 million children, have disabling hearing loss requiring rehabilitation; threshold is greater than 35 dB in the better-hearing ear. Also reports 95.1 million children aged 5-19 with hearing loss of any degree; neither figure is a caption or sign-language-use count.

title: International Day of Sign Languages
claim_scope: Reports the World Federation of the Deaf estimate of more than 70 million deaf people, over 80% in developing countries, using more than 300 sign languages; International Sign has limited international use and is not a universal instructional language.

title: Marrakesh Treaty to Facilitate Access to Published Works for Persons Who Are Blind, Visually Impaired or Otherwise Print Disabled
claim_scope: Articles 2-3 provide functional definitions of beneficiary persons and accessible-format copies; the legal category overlaps vision, perceptual/reading, motor, and other limitations and supplies no global prevalence estimate.

title: Prevalence of Developmental Dyslexia in Primary School Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
claim_scope: Random-effects pooled primary-school prevalence 7.10%, 95% CI 6.27%-7.97%, from studies searched through June 2021; I-squared 97.6% and results vary with operational definition, so the rate is not an all-age global headcount.

title: Prevalence of intellectual disability: a meta-analysis of population-based studies
claim_scope: Pooled prevalence 10.37 per 1,000 population, 95% CI 9.55-11.18, from 52 studies published 1980-2009; definitions, ascertainment, setting, age mix, and country-income mix varied.

title: Dementia
claim_scope: 57 million people had dementia in 2021, more than 60% in low- and middle-income countries, with nearly 10 million new cases annually; contextual older-adult cognitive-access anchor, not a format preference.

title: Literacy
claim_scope: 739 million adults aged 15+ lacked basic literacy skills and two-thirds were women; global data are largely self- or proxy-declared and may understate functional difficulty.

title: International Literacy Day 2025 brief
claim_scope: Corroborates the 2025 adult-literacy figure and its gender distribution; literacy is a coarse threshold distinct from digital skill, subject vocabulary, disability, and second-language proficiency.

title: Facts and Figures 2025
claim_scope: Modelled 2025 estimates: 6.0 billion people (74%) used the Internet and 2.2 billion remained offline; use was 85% urban versus 58% rural and 94% in high-income versus 23% in low-income countries; 96% of offline people lived in low- and middle-income countries.

title: Global number of Internet users increases, but disparities deepen key digital divides
claim_scope: Press release for Facts and Figures 2025 and notice that global and regional modelled estimates may be revised as Member State data improve.

title: Facts and Figures 2025 presentation and definition note
claim_scope: Defines an Internet user as a person who used the Internet in the previous three months; this differs from coverage, household access, subscription, device ownership, or skill.

title: Mobile network coverage
claim_scope: 2025 coverage: 4G reached 93% and 5G 55% of the world population; 4G was 99% urban versus 84% rural, while 38% of rural residents in low-income countries had 4G; coverage does not establish use, affordability, device, or skill.

title: Facts and Figures 2025 methodology
claim_scope: Definitions and modelling notes for Internet use, coverage, affordability, and related indicators; preserves distinctions among measured constructs.

title: Affordability of ICT services
claim_scope: Median 5-GB data-only mobile basket cost 1.4% of GNI per capita globally in 2025; low-income subscribers paid about 22 times the income share paid in high-income economies; these are price ratios, not population counts.

title: Mobile phone ownership
claim_scope: In 2024, four in five people aged 10+ owned a mobile phone, versus 56% in low-income economies; mobile phone includes feature phones, and ownership is not equivalent to smartphone capability, unshared access, or Internet use.

title: How many children and young people have internet access at home?
claim_scope: Historical 2020 stage-specific anchor: 1.3 billion children aged 3-17 (67%) and 759 million people aged 15-24 (63%) lacked Internet at home; household access is not individual use or school connectivity.

title: Two thirds of the world's school-age children have no internet access at home
claim_scope: Regional tables and definitions accompanying the dated 2020 home-connectivity estimates; not a current post-growth denominator.

title: Almost one billion children and adults with disabilities and older persons in need of assistive technology denied access, according to new report
claim_scope: More than 2.5 billion people need one or more assistive products and nearly 1 billion were denied access; need met ranged from 3% in poorer countries to 90% in wealthy countries in a 35-country analysis.

title: Global report on assistive technology
claim_scope: Full report supporting assistive-technology need and access estimates; product category spans vision, hearing, mobility, cognition, communication, self-care, and software and is broader than screen readers or braille devices.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
claim_scope: Normative web-accessibility standard supporting semantic alternatives, keyboard access, captions, audio description, reflow, target sizing, and other testable success criteria; conformance is not itself evidence of educational efficacy.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.10: Reflow
claim_scope: Explains reflow without loss of information or functionality at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels, subject to criterion exceptions.

title: Understanding Success Criterion 2.5.8: Target Size (Minimum)
claim_scope: Explains the 24-by-24-CSS-pixel minimum pointer-target criterion and spacing and other exceptions.

title: EPUB 3.3
claim_scope: W3C Recommendation defining the EPUB 3.3 container, structured web content, navigation, and media overlays that associate XHTML content with prerecorded audio.

title: EPUB Accessibility 1.1
claim_scope: Defines EPUB accessibility conformance and metadata; formal floor is WCAG 2.0 Level A while strongly recommending the latest WCAG 2 at Level AA, so implementations must state actual version and level.

title: DAISY Format
claim_scope: Describes structured navigation and synchronized full text/audio supporting speech, enlargement, refreshable braille, and navigable long-form reading.

title: ISO 24495-1:2023 Plain language - Part 1: Governing principles and guidelines
claim_scope: General plain-language principles for primarily textual documents; principles apply broadly but examples are English, so target-language rewriting and validation remain necessary.

title: Making Content Usable for People with Cognitive and Learning Disabilities
claim_scope: Supplemental guidance on common words, short sentences and blocks, literal language, summaries, images, predictable interaction, error recovery, and reduced memory demand; guidance goes beyond WCAG conformance.

title: World Braille Usage, Third Edition
organization: Perkins, Library of Congress National Library Service, and International Council on English Braille
claim_scope: Documents 133 languages represented by 137 alphabet-and-punctuation braille codes, with country variation; technical subjects may require additional math or music conventions.

title: Braille Resources for Transcribers and Teachers of Braille
organization: Library of Congress National Library Service
claim_scope: Authoritative resource index for braille transcription and specialist codes; supports the requirement to declare and verify language and subject codes rather than treating braille as universal.

title: Accessible Books Consortium
claim_scope: Recognizes accessible publishing formats including braille, audio, e-text, and large print; does not provide a global user denominator.

title: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Article 9: Accessibility
claim_scope: Requires access to the physical environment, transportation, information and communications, including ICT, and other facilities and services in urban and rural areas.

title: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, Article 24: Education
claim_scope: Requires inclusive education and lifelong learning and names braille, alternative script, augmentative and alternative communication, sign language, appropriate languages and modes, trained staff, tertiary, vocational, and adult education.

title: MathML
organization: DAISY Consortium Accessible Publishing Knowledge Base
claim_scope: Recommends MathML as the most accessible equation representation where supported, notes older EPUB reading-system variation, and calls for extended descriptions for complex image fallbacks.

title: Math Working Group Charter
claim_scope: Reports all major browser engines supporting MathML Core from 2023 and scopes continuing MathML 4 and accessibility work; browser support does not remove language-specific speech/braille testing.

title: Accessible Digital Textbooks for All
claim_scope: Practical educational model combining structured text, narration, local sign-language video, captions, image descriptions, simplified text, adjustable display, and interactivity with learner-selectable features.

title: User requirements
organization: UNICEF Accessible Digital Textbooks for All
claim_scope: Calls for a fluent local sign-language presenter, conceptually accurate rather than word-for-word translation, and synchronization of sign video to the corresponding passage; also documents selectable accessibility features.

title: Producing sign language videos
organization: UNICEF Accessible Digital Textbooks for All
claim_scope: Production guidance for local sign-language recordings, including signer fluency, framing, face/hands/torso visibility, contrast, synchronization, and concept fidelity.

title: Audiobooks
claim_scope: W3C Recommendation for accessible audiobook packaging and navigation, including an offline/download path rather than streaming-only access.

title: Charter for Public Digital Learning Platforms: Working Document
organization: UNESCO, UNICEF, and International Telecommunication Union
claim_scope: Calls for low-cost hardware support, intermittent/low-bandwidth operation, and downloadable public digital-learning content; working document status should be preserved.

title: ICT skills
claim_scope: Overall at-least-basic-skills data were available for only eight countries, with a 16%-74% range among Internet users; evidence of a measurement gap, not a global prevalence estimate.
